sections.title: Hezekiah's Invitation to the Passover
observations: King Hezekiah, seeking to restore true worship in Judah, sends out invitations to all Israel and Judah to celebrate the Passover in Jerusalem. This act signifies a desire for national unity and a return to covenant faithfulness.
The invitation is extended not only to the people of Judah but also to the remnants of Israel, highlighting Hezekiah's hope for reconciliation among the divided kingdoms.

sections.title: The Response to the Invitation
observations: Despite the king's earnest invitation, many mocked and scorned the messengers. This reflects the spiritual apathy and division that had taken root in Israel.
However, some from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem, demonstrating that there was still a remnant willing to respond to God's call.

sections.title: Preparation for the Passover
observations: The people who gathered in Jerusalem prepared for the Passover, even though it was not observed at the appointed time due to their previous neglect of the law.
Hezekiah prayed for the people, asking God to pardon those who were not ceremonially clean, showing his understanding of God's grace and mercy.

sections.title: The Celebration of the Passover
observations: The Passover was celebrated with great joy, and the people worshipped God with sincerity. This event marked a significant spiritual revival in the nation.
The participation of the Levites and priests was crucial in leading the worship and ensuring that the sacrifices were made according to the law.

importantVerses.commentary: Hezekiah encourages the people to return to the Lord, promising that if they do, He will return to them. This verse emphasizes God's willingness to forgive and restore those who seek Him.
Hezekiah's prayer for the people who were not clean shows the importance of intercession and God's grace in accepting those who come to Him with sincere hearts.

questions: What does Hezekiah's invitation to the Passover reveal about his leadership and priorities as king?
How does the response of the people to the invitation reflect the spiritual state of Israel at that time?
What can we learn from Hezekiah's prayer for those who were not ceremonially clean?
In what ways does this chapter illustrate the themes of grace and restoration in the Old Testament?
